references.text: Peter denies that anyone intentionally touched Jesus, but Jesus insists that someone touched him—this is the immediate context for Jesus' statement in verse 46.
Power went out from Jesus and healed everyone—the same expression for power (δύναμις) going out from Jesus is used here.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus notices that power has gone out from him when the woman touched his cloak.
Matthew's parallel account of the woman who touched Jesus' cloak and was healed.
All who touched the edge of Jesus' cloak were healed—this shows that healing power went out from Jesus through physical contact.
The woman touched Jesus' clothes and immediately felt she had been healed—a parallel to the touch that Jesus perceives in Luke 8:46.
The Lord's power was present so that Jesus could heal—showing that healing power (δύναμις) was at work through Jesus.
God anointed Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power (δύναμις), and he went around healing—confirming that divine power worked through him.
Peter's words about God's power (δύναμις) working through faith—a parallel to the connection between faith and power going out from Jesus.
